title: containers.Map
summary: Create key-value dictionary objects in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Map storage and outputs are host-resident. Resident constructor, key-query, removal, lookup, selected-values, and assignment inputs are gated RunMat extensions that gather before host Map processing.

description: `containers.Map` creates host-resident handle objects that associate unique character or real numeric keys with values. Public key types are `char`, `double`, `single`, `int32`, `uint32`, `int64`, and `uint64`; declared value types include `any`, `char`, `logical`, both floating classes, and all eight integer classes.
behaviors: Constructor keys must be unique and duplicates raise an error. Later assignment to an existing key overwrites the stored value.
The read-only `KeyType`, `ValueType`, and `Count` properties are readable with dot-indexing; `Count` is a uint64 scalar.
`map(key)` returns the associated value; requesting a missing key raises the MATLAB-compatible error *"The specified key is not present in this container."*
Assignments of the form `map(key) = value` update or insert entries.

RunMat returns `keys(map)` as a sorted row cell and aligns `values(map)` to that order, matching public examples without treating ordering as a formal MATLAB guarantee. `values(map,keySet)` requires a cell key set and preserves its shape.
`isKey` returns scalar logical for one scalar key and a same-shape logical result for key collections; `remove` mutates the handle and has no public output.
Integer key identity is exact for int32, uint32, int64, and uint64, including values wider than binary64 can distinguish. Narrow integer key arrays reject rather than alias through double.

All eight integer value classes preserve native storage through construction, assignment, lookup, and values output. Declared integer ValueType values are scalar and use the runtime's MATLAB integer saturation rules; ValueType any retains nonscalar integer arrays exactly.
`UniformValues` defaults to true for populated constructors; specifying false permits heterogeneous values and sets ValueType to `any`.

MATLAB documents thread-based execution but no gpuArray capability for this class. RunMat resident input gathering is therefore compatibility-gated and always produces host Map state and host outputs.

faqs.question: Which key types are supported?
faqs.answer: Public KeyType values are `'char'`, `'double'`, `'single'`, `'int32'`, `'uint32'`, `'int64'`, and `'uint64'`. String-array constructor keys are converted to character-vector keys, so the resulting KeyType is `'char'`; logical and narrow integer KeyType values are not public Map key types.

faqs.question: What happens when I provide duplicate keys at construction time?
faqs.answer: Duplicate keys raise the same error as MATLAB: *"Duplicate key name was provided."* During assignment, duplicate keys overwrite the existing value.

faqs.question: Does RunMat honour `'UniformValues', true`?
faqs.answer: Yes. When this option is set, RunMat enforces that each inserted value matches the MATLAB class of the first value. Retrieval still uses cell arrays, mirroring MATLAB when `'ValueType'` is `'any'`.

faqs.question: Can I store GPU arrays as map values?
faqs.answer: Only as a RunMat extension. MATLAB does not document gpuArray support for containers.Map. With RunMat extensions enabled, resident keys or values gather before processing and the Map stores host values; strict compatibility mode rejects before provider access.

faqs.question: How does `length(map)` behave?
faqs.answer: `length(map)` returns the number of stored keys (identical to the `Count` property). `size(map)` remains `[1 1]`, matching MATLAB's handle semantics.

faqs.question: What error is raised when a key is missing?
faqs.answer: Indexing a missing key produces the MATLAB-compatible error message *"The specified key is not present in this container."*

faqs.question: Does the map preserve insertion order?
faqs.answer: No insertion-order guarantee should be assumed. RunMat returns keys in key order and aligns `values(map)` to that order, matching the ordering shown by MATLAB's public examples.

faqs.question: How do I remove every entry?
faqs.answer: Call `remove(map, keys(map))` or reassign a new empty map. RunMat currently keeps the internal storage until the handle is cleared, matching MATLAB's lifetime semantics.

faqs.question: What happens if I pass a non-scalar key?
faqs.answer: Keys must be scalar. Passing vectors, matrices, or nested cell arrays of keys raises a descriptive error pointing to the offending argument.

faqs.question: How do I create an empty `containers.Map`?
faqs.answer: — Call the constructor with no arguments: `m = containers.Map()`. This yields an empty map with the default `'char'` KeyType and `'any'` ValueType. To pin the types up front (so the first insertion can't change them), supply them explicitly: `m = containers.Map('KeyType', 'char', 'ValueType', 'double')`. Either form gives you a map you can populate via `m(key) = value`.

faqs.question: What is the default KeyType and ValueType?
faqs.answer: — The default `KeyType` is `'char'` and the default `ValueType` is `'any'`. That is why `containers.Map()` with no arguments accepts character-vector keys and arbitrary values. To use numeric keys (for example `double` or `int32`) or to restrict values to a specific class, set `'KeyType'`/`'ValueType'` at construction time — they become read-only properties afterwards.

faqs.question: Can I use MATLAB `string` values as `containers.Map` keys?
faqs.answer: String arrays are accepted as constructor key sets and converted to character vectors, making the resulting KeyType `'char'`. Key lookup methods also accept a string scalar as a textual key, but `'string'` is not a KeyType value.

faqs.question: Is `containers.Map` a handle class?
faqs.answer: — Yes. `containers.Map` inherits from `handle`, so maps have **reference semantics**: if you assign `m2 = m1`, both variables point to the same underlying map and mutations through either handle are visible through the other. To get an independent copy, rebuild the map from `keys(m1)` and `values(m1)` (for example, `m2 = containers.Map(keys(m1), values(m1))`). MATLAB does not expose a public `copy` method on `containers.Map`.

gpu_behavior: The data structure itself resides on the CPU. RunMat can gather resident inputs only through explicitly gated extensions; Maps never retain device buffers and all method outputs are host-resident.

example.input:
m = containers.Map()
m = containers.Map(keys, values)
m = containers.Map(keys, values, 'UniformValues', tf)
m = containers.Map('KeyType', ktype, 'ValueType', vtype)

points: `keys` is a cell vector (or string array) of scalar keys. Every element must share the same `KeyType`; mixing classes raises an error.
`values` is a matched cell vector of the values to store, one per key. When `'UniformValues'` is `true`, every value must share the same MATLAB class.
`ktype` selects `'char'`, `'double'`, `'single'`, `'int32'`, `'uint32'`, `'int64'`, or `'uint64'`. Empty typed construction requires both KeyType and ValueType.
`vtype` selects `'any'`, `'char'`, `'logical'`, `'double'`, `'single'`, or any of the eight integer classes.
Returns `m`, a handle to a `containers.Map` object. Because it is a handle class, assigning `m2 = m` produces two references to the same map.
